title: 第0020章 星际航行第026章 青龙献宝
slug: 全民修仙之系统上交囯家
content_zh:
华纪56年7月1日至5日，星际空间，“华夏之星”号旗舰。
连续的空间跳跃让时间变得模糊。
张德华已经分不清现在是白天还是黑夜——在星际空间中，没有白天黑夜之分，只有永恒的黑暗和远处几点微弱的星光。“华夏之星”号舰内的人工照明系统模拟着修仙星球的昼夜节律，但那只是模拟，不是真实。
“第二次跳跃完成。”导航官汇报，“当前位置，距离修仙星球一千零三光年。距离天狼星系外围，还有两次跳跃。”
张德华站在星图前，看着那条从修仙星球延伸到天狼星系的红色航线。一千光年，对于人类来说是一个难以想象的数字。光需要走一千年才能到达的距离，他们的舰队只用了几秒钟。
但即使是这样，他们仍然需要多次跳跃才能到达目标。
“为什么不能一次跳到？”陈铁军问过这个问题。
“能量。”能源官回答，“空间跳跃的能量消耗与距离成正比。五百光年是当前引擎的经济航程，再远的话，能源储备会不够支撑返程。”
“所以我们只能分段跳。”
“对。像青蛙一样，一次跳不远，但多跳几次总能到。”
张德华听到这个比喻时忍不住笑了。青蛙远征军，倒也贴切。
7月2日，舰队在星际空间休整。
所有战舰关闭主引擎，以惯性滑行。舷窗外什么都没有——没有星星，没有行星，连尘埃都看不到。只有无尽的黑暗，和无尽的虚空。
“这就是星际空间。”陈铁军站在张德华身边，“比任何沙漠都要荒凉。”
“但也比任何地方都要广阔。”张德华说，“广阔到可以装下整个华夏文明。”
他下令全体将士在休整期间进行适应性训练。太空陆战队在“华夏之星”号的模拟训练舱中进行零重力环境下的战术演练，舰员们进行空间跳跃后的设备检修，科研团队分析探测卫星传回的星际空间数据。
“首长，我们发现了一个有趣的东西。”林薇的声音从通讯频道传来。
“什么？”
“在距离舰队零点三光年的位置，有一个微型黑洞。不大，质量只有太阳的十分之一。”
“有威胁吗？”

“没有。距离足够远，引力影响可以忽略不计。但这个发现很有价值——这说明这片星域的天体分布比我们预想的要复杂。”
张德华点头：“标记坐标，继续观测。”
7月3日，舰队进行第三次空间跳跃。
这一次，跳跃距离增加到了五百五十光年——能源官说可以试试更远的距离，节省一次跳跃次数。
跳跃成功。舰队完好无损。
“当前距离修仙星球，一千五百五十光年。”导航官汇报，“距离天狼星系，还有一次跳跃。”
“很好。”张德华说，“明天进行最后一次跳跃，到达天狼星系外围。”
但在这之前，他还有一件事要做。
“全体注意。”他拿起通讯器，声音传遍每一艘战舰，“我是张德华。明天我们将到达天狼星系，进入外星文明的控制区域。在此之前，我要检阅部队。”
他顿了顿。
“不是形式主义的检阅。我要看看，我们的远征军是不是真的准备好了。”
检阅在“华夏之星”号的机库举行。
一万名将士再次列队。但这一次，他们不是站在平地上——机库的引力模拟系统关闭了，所有人都悬浮在半空中，依靠自身的修为和装备保持姿态。
这是张德华的要求。在星际空间中，重力是奢侈品。真正的战斗可能在零重力环境下进行，适应不了零重力的战士，不配称为星际远征军。
五千名太空陆战队员首先接受检阅。
他们在零重力环境中如鱼得水，利用喷气背包和自身修为在机库中快速移动、变换队形、进行战术演练。他们的动作精准而迅速，没有丝毫拖泥带水。
“报告首长！”陆战队指挥官大声道，“太空陆战队五千人，全部适应零重力环境！随时可以投入战斗！”
张德华点头：“很好。”
三千名舰员接受检阅。他们展示的是战舰操控能力——在模拟系统中，舰员们同时操控十二艘战舰进行编队飞行、紧急规避、火力协同。所有操作一气呵成，误差率低于百分之零点一。
一千名科研团队接受检阅。他们展示的是快速分析能力——在十分钟内，他们对一颗未知小行星的样本进行了全面分析，得出了成分、结构、形成年代等数据，准确率百分之九十九点七。

一千名后勤保障团队接受检阅。他们展示的是野战维修能力——在模拟的“战舰受损”场景中，后勤团队在十五分钟内完成了舰体修复、能源补给、伤员救治等一系列任务。
检阅结束后，张德华站在所有人面前。
“同志们。”他说，“你们的训练成果，我很满意。但我必须提醒你们——星际空间不是修仙星球，这里没有规则，没有法律，没有道德。这里只有弱肉强食，只有生存和毁灭。”
他的声音变得严肃。
content_en:
July 1st to 5th, 56th Chinese Year, interstellar space, the flagship "China Star".
Continuous space jumps make time blur.
Zhang Dehua can no longer tell whether it is day or night - in interstellar space, there is no distinction between day and night, only eternal darkness and a few faint starlights in the distance. The artificial lighting system inside the "China Star" simulates the circadian rhythm of the Immortal Planet, but it is only a simulation, not reality.
"The second jump is completed." The navigation officer reported, "The current position is one thousand and three light years away from the Immortal Planet. There are still two jumps away from the outer reaches of the Sirius Galaxy."
Zhang Dehua stood in front of the star map, looking at the red route extending from the Immortal Planet to the Sirius Galaxy. One thousand light years is an unimaginable number for humans. The distance that light would have taken a thousand years to travel, their fleet traveled in just a few seconds.
But even then, they still need to jump multiple times to reach their target.
"Why can't you jump in one go?" Chen Tiejun asked this question.
"Energy." The energy officer replied, "The energy consumption of a space jump is proportional to the distance. Five hundred light years is the economic range of the current engine. If it is any further, the energy reserve will not be enough to support the return journey."
"So we can only jump in sections."
"Yes. Like a frog, you can't reach far in one jump, but you can always reach it if you jump a few times."
Zhang Dehua couldn't help laughing when he heard this metaphor. The Frog Expeditionary Force is quite appropriate.
On July 2, the fleet rested in interstellar space.
All battleships shut down their main engines and coasted. There was nothing outside the portholes—no stars, no planets, not even dust. There is only endless darkness and endless emptiness.
"This is interstellar space." Chen Tiejun stood next to Zhang Dehua. "It is more desolate than any desert."
"But it is broader than anywhere else." Zhang Dehua said, "It is so vast that it can contain the entire Chinese civilization."
He ordered all soldiers to conduct adaptive training during the rest period. The Space Marine Corps conducts tactical drills in a zero-gravity environment in the simulated training module of the "China Star". The crew conducts equipment maintenance after space jumps, and the scientific research team analyzes the interstellar space data returned by the detection satellite.
"Chief, we found something interesting." Lin Wei's voice came from the communication channel.
"What?"
"There is a miniature black hole 0.3 light years away from the fleet. It is not big, and its mass is only one-tenth of the sun."
"Is there a threat?"
"No. The distance is far enough that the gravitational influence is negligible. But this discovery is very valuable - it shows that the distribution of celestial bodies in this star field is more complex than we expected."
Zhang Dehua nodded: "Mark the coordinates and continue observing."
On July 3, the fleet made its third space jump.
This time, the jump distance was increased to 550 light years - the energy officer said that he could try a longer distance and save one jump.
The jump was successful. The fleet was intact.
"The current distance is 1,550 light years from the Immortal Planet." The navigation officer reported, "There is still one jump to the Sirius Galaxy."
"Very good." Zhang Dehua said, "We will make the last jump tomorrow and reach the outer reaches of the Sirius galaxy."
But before that, he had one more thing to do.
"Attention everyone." He picked up the communicator and his voice spread to every battleship. "I am Zhang Dehua. Tomorrow we will arrive at the Sirius galaxy and enter the area controlled by alien civilization. Before that, I want to review the troops."
He paused.
"This is not a formal review. I want to see if our expeditionary force is really ready."
The review was held in the hangar of the "China Star".
Ten thousand soldiers lined up again. But this time, they were not standing on flat ground - the gravity simulation system of the hangar was turned off, and everyone was suspended in mid-air, relying on their own cultivation andEquipment maintains posture.
This is Zhang Dehua's request. In interstellar space, gravity is a luxury. Real battles may take place in a zero-gravity environment. Soldiers who cannot adapt to zero-gravity are not worthy of being called an interstellar expeditionary force.
Five thousand Space Marines were reviewed first.
They are at home in the zero-gravity environment, using jetpacks and their own abilities to move quickly in the hangar, change formations, and conduct tactical drills. Their movements were precise and swift, without any sloppiness.
"Report to the chief!" the Marine Corps commander shouted, "There are five thousand Space Marines, all adapted to the zero-gravity environment! They are ready to go into battle at any time!"
Zhang Dehua nodded: "Very good."
Three thousand sailors were inspected. What they demonstrated was the ability to control warships - in the simulation system, the crew simultaneously controlled twelve warships for formation flight, emergency evasion, and firepower coordination. All operations are done in one go, with an error rate of less than 0.1 percent.
A thousand scientific research teams were inspected. What they demonstrated was their rapid analysis capabilities - within ten minutes, they conducted a comprehensive analysis of a sample of an unknown asteroid and obtained data such as composition, structure, formation age, etc., with an accuracy of 99.7%.
One thousand logistics support teams were inspected. What they demonstrated was field maintenance capabilities - in a simulated "battleship damage" scenario, the logistics team completed a series of tasks such as hull repair, energy supply, and casualty treatment within fifteen minutes.
After the review, Zhang Dehua stood in front of everyone.
"Comrades," he said, "I am very satisfied with your training results. But I must remind you - interstellar space is not a planet for cultivating immortals. There are no rules, no laws, and no morals here. There is only the law of the jungle, only survival and destruction."
His voice became serious.
